Logan / team —

Thanks for the ping and the background. Below are suggested approaches and sample redline text you can send to Brightline. I kept the language narrow to minimize open-ended liability while being responsive to their ask. High-level points:

- Defense vs. reimbursement: Redwood will offer to assume defense of third-party IP claims only to the extent the claim arises from Redwood-owned model code, model weights, or deployment infrastructure. For claims that arise from customer-provided prompts, data, or customer-managed keys, Redwood will reimburse reasonable costs but will not assume defense.

- Evidence handback SLA: we can commit to producing relevant logs and evidence within 10 business days of a written request, subject to preservation scope (we preserve request/response logs for 90 days by default; extended retention is an add-on). If evidence requires forensic reconstruction beyond logs (e.g., reconstructing input data that was not persisted), we will cooperate but may require an extended timeline and pass-through costs.

- Keystore/HSM carveout: proposed clause: "Customer manages keys and grants Redwood only the minimum cryptographic operations required for service execution. Redwood will not have access to plaintext protected by Customer keys and shall have no liability for Customer key compromise or misuse, except to the extent such compromise results from Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct."

Sample redline excerpt (can paste into the Order Form):

1. Indemnity 

(a) Redwood Indemnity. Subject to the limitations below, Redwood will defend Customer against third-party claims alleging that the Redwood services, as delivered under this Order Form, infringe a third party’s issued patent, copyright or trademark, and will pay those final, adjudicated damages and settlement amounts. Redwood’s obligation to defend is limited to claims that arise solely from (i) Redwood’s model code or model weights; or (ii) Redwood’s deployment infrastructure.

(b) Customer Obligations. Customer will (i) promptly notify Redwood in writing of any claim; (ii) provide reasonable cooperation and access to relevant evidence; and (iii) permit Redwood sole control of the defense and settlement of such claim (provided that Redwood may not settle any claim that imposes an obligation on Customer without Customer’s prior written consent).

(c) Reimbursement carveout. For claims that arise from Customer-provided prompts, data, third-party integrations, or Customer-managed keys, Redwood’s obligation will be limited to reimbursement of reasonable defense costs and settlements, capped at the Order Form total for services for the preceding 12 months, unless otherwise agreed.

2. Evidence handback and preservation

(a) Redwood will produce available logs and recordings necessary to evaluate a claim within ten (10) business days of a written request, in a mutually-agreeable electronic format.

(b) If reconstructive analysis is required, Redwood will propose scope and estimated costs within five (5) business days and complete the work on a time-and-materials basis.

3. Keystore/HSM limitation

(a) Customer keys. Customer will be responsible for key management; Redwood will only perform cryptographic operations as authorized by Customer and will not have access to plaintext material protected by Customer keys. Redwood is not responsible for loss or compromise of Customer-managed keys, except in the event of Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct.

Operational notes / risks:
- Ten business days for evidence is operationally reasonable for logs; forensic reconstruction can take longer. If Brightline wants absolute guarantees for reconstructability of deleted inputs, that will require a product change / retention add-on.
- The reimbursement cap language above is negotiable but avoids open-ended exposure. Legal recommends keeping caps tied to the Order Form value.

Next steps: 
1) If sales is comfortable with the cap and 10-day evidence SLA, send this to Brightline and ask for their counter.
2) If Brightline pushes for broader indemnity (AI output included without carveouts), escalate to AM/Head of Sales for a pricing concession.

I attached our standard indemnity template for reference. Happy to hop on a quick call with Brightline legal if needed.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
